implementation_notes: The standard library has no pub-sub primitive: the idiomatic realization is a registry of std::function callbacks protected by std::mutex, dispatching a copy of the event to each subscriber after taking a snapshot. This is the dependency-free default (C++11 and later) and keeps fan-out, snapshot and overflow policy under explicit control.
pitfalls: Dispatching under std::mutex serializes subscribers and deadlocks on re-entrant subscribe or publish; snapshot first, then call outside the lock.
A subscriber lambda capturing this of a destroyed object is the classic dangling-callback bug; track lifetimes (weak_ptr, explicit unsubscribe) instead of relying on raw captures.
std::function may allocate on every subscribe and copy; keep the hot publish path free of allocations by storing stable nodes or a vector of callables reserved ahead.

variants.name: Boost.Signals2 signal/slot
variants.implementation_notes: Boost.Signals2 supplies the channel as a managed signals and slots system: the signal is the publisher, connected slots are the subscribers (thread-safe in the Signals2 variant), and connections are objects that disconnect on destruction. Choose it when automatic connection management and thread-safe emission outweigh the Boost dependency; prefer the std::function registry when the project forbids or does not already use Boost.
pitfalls: The signal is a value the publisher owns and the slots outlive; destroying the signal disconnects everything, and a slot capturing dead state still runs until its connection dies.
Signals2 is thread-safe but not lock-free: emitting while holding another mutex invites lock-order inversions with slot code.
